item.title: Solvent heterogeneity regulates assembly pathways in supramolecular polymerization
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78525-6

Supramolecular polymers often require solvent mixtures for their preparation but their impact on supramolecular polymerization remains poorly understood. Here, the authors demonstrate that solvent heterogeneity biases assembly pathways in supramolecular polymerization, with the extent of this effect determined by monomer structure.

item.title: Bacteroides–Escherichia interactions contribute to colonization resistance against Clostridioides difficile
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78132-5

Here the authors demonstrate that interactions between Bacteroides and Escherichia shape resistance to Clostridioides difficile and identify ecological and metabolic signatures with the potential to guide microbiome-based therapies.

item.title: Molecular architecture of Cryptococcus cell walls reveals species-specific chitosan-dependent remodeling
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78940-9

This study reveals distinct cell-wall organization in two pathogenic Cryptococcus species, revealing that chitosan loss triggers species-specific structural remodeling that may influence host interactions.
